Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Start the live HL build by reading users and tasks from JSON-backed storage and rendering them through the same interface pattern used in SL. You are rebuilding the same feature with JSON storage, so keep the user experience aligned while the persistence model changes.

The key idea for this feature is Backend parity, read routes, and predictable rendering from document data.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
GET requestA request used to retrieve existing data.
JSON responseStructured data returned to the browser.
Render functionA function that turns returned data into visible output.
Request cycleThe path from browser action to response and redraw.

Why this still matters to the client

  • The client still needs a readable task list and a populated assignee control. The storage model changed, but the user-facing promise did not.
  • This page proves the same interface can sit on top of a different backend if the response contract stays clear.

What to carry in from earlier pages

  • Bring forward the SQL lesson on render targets and empty states.
  • Use the modelling comparison page to explain why usernames may need to be looked up or attached during the backend read.

Backend terms to notice

  • @app.route() tells Flask which URL a function responds to.
  • methods=["GET"] says the route is for reading data.
  • jsonify() returns structured JSON to the browser.

Rendered task list preview

After the read request succeeds, the user should see a list that looks deliberate rather than raw.

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • The browser needs structured data back from the server before it can draw the list.
  • Keep the rendering logic in one place so the display stays consistent.
  • A good empty state is part of the feature, not an afterthought.
  • Reading JSON-backed data often means loading a document structure and then preparing a browser-friendly response.

Generic fetch pattern

function loadItems() {
  fetch("/api/items")
    .then((response) => response.json())
    .then((items) => renderItems(items));
}
fetch()

Starts an HTTP request from the browser to the backend.

response

This variable holds the raw HTTP response object before the JSON is extracted.

response.json()

Turns the JSON response body into usable JavaScript data.

=>

An arrow function is a short way to write a function you pass into `.then()`.

Build it in this order

Keep the frontend contract stable while the backend swaps to JSON file reads.

Step 1 app.py

Write the read helper functions first

  • Create one helper to load users and one to load tasks from JSON files.
  • Decide what should happen if the tasks file does not exist yet.
  • Explain why these helpers belong above the route functions.
Step 2 app.py

Write the `/users` and `/tasks` routes

  • Return JSON from the users route first because it is the simpler one.
  • Then build the task route and decide how each task will gain a readable username for the UI.
  • Keep the response shape aligned with the SQL version so the browser code stays familiar.

Ask yourself

  • Where does the username come from if the task object only stores an id?
  • Why is backend parity useful when comparing storage models?
Step 3 static/js/app.js

Reuse the browser read pattern

  • Write the same fetch, response.json, and render sequence the SQL track used.
  • Prove the list and assignee control both redraw from backend data.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
app.pyHolds the JSON-backed GET routesLoad the files, prepare the response, and return JSON
static/js/app.jsDraws the list and fills the assignee controlReuse the read-and-render browser pattern
data/users.json and data/tasks.jsonHold the stored document dataKeep both files valid and readable

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • The `/users` and `/tasks` routes return sensible JSON.
  • The browser draws the list from real backend data.
  • The interface still feels aligned with the SQL version.
